reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point in Sansepolcro, Italy, tagged as a data center is probably a mistag for an IT reseller, not a compute facility.

The record carries no power figure, no operator, and no website. Its own reading concludes that the name WinEuropa, combining "Win" with "Europa," points to a regional software or PC sales and support business, and that such businesses keep modest office IT rather than running colocation or cloud capacity for outside customers. The tag says data center; nothing else in the data does.

For AI scaling this is a negative result, and a useful one. A map of data centers assembled from volunteered geographic tags will contain points that are offices, resellers, or clerical errors, and each one inflates the apparent count of facilities without adding a megawatt. The absence of a capacity value here is consistent with that: there is nothing to measure.

What the data does not establish is that WinEuropa is not a data center. The research status is exhausted, meaning the check was cut short by search limits rather than completed. The determination is name-based and probable, not verified. The only firm facts are the coordinates, the tag, the name, and a nearest airport 37.6 miles away in Perugia.
